reason: The text predominantly portrays the general Israelite population negatively. They are characterized as covenant-breakers who have destroyed God's altars and killed His prophets (הָרְג֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב אֶת־ נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ). They are depicted as engaged in Baal worship, with Elijah lamenting that the people have abandoned the covenant. While there are notable exceptions—the 7,000 faithful remnant who have not bowed to Baal, and Elisha who is portrayed very favorably in immediately abandoning his livelihood to follow Elijah—these represent exceptions to the broader negative characterization. The dominant portrayal of regular people in this passage is unfavorable.
